issues.body: Section 3 infers that the pinned verifier already performs asynchronous, SSRF-guarded DNS resolution solely because Cargo.lock lists hickory-resolver, and calls dependency presence "exactly the property the repin existed to produce." A dependency can be unused on the relevant path, used only under another configuration, or wrapped without the claimed SSRF policy. The cargo-vet note is also explicitly acknowledged as an unverified pre-existing assertion, so it cannot independently close this evidence gap. This leaves the NO PORT capability verdict for chore/repin-async-dns-verifier unsupported.
issues.fix_hint: Inspect the pinned solid-oidc-verifier revision and cite the concrete WebID/issuer resolution call path showing that the network feature invokes the async hickory resolver with the claimed SSRF protections, plus a relevant test if one exists. If that source/path cannot be inspected, defer this capability-level verdict alongside the branch-level verdict instead of treating Cargo.lock membership as proof.
issues.title: Dependency presence does not establish the verifier repin capability

verdict.summary: The round-1 branch-level DROP overclaim has been corrected: the record now consistently defers branch deletion and limits its conclusion to capability-level subsumption. However, the verifier-repin capability conclusion is still not established by the evidence cited. Cargo.lock proves only that hickory-resolver is in the pinned package's dependency graph; it does not prove that the verifier actually uses it for WebID/issuer resolution, that this path is asynchronous, or that the relevant resolver path is SSRF-guarded. Because that unsupported inference is the sole basis for declaring the repin capability subsumed and doing no port, the record is not yet complete.
